statement: Every existing positive integral witness at prime p congruent to 1 modulo 12 satisfies the explicit inverse, second-compound, third-compound, and determinant-inverse bounds with gamma=80/6279^4.
The third receiver singular value exceeds sqrt(gamma/180), so at most one inverse singular direction can be unbounded.
proof: core.tex, Theorem 1.1 and the final paragraph of Section 3

statement: Two infinite prime families in p congruent to 13 modulo 24 attain the p^(3/2), p^0, and p^(-2) inverse-compound exponents with the displayed leading constants.
dependencies: Dirichlet theorem for the reduced class 13 modulo 24

statement: On four distinct positive labelled roots, the receiver is invertible exactly when h is nonzero; at h=0 it has rank exactly three with the displayed kernel generator and cokernel hyperplane.
The four singular values, inverse rank-one limit, and finite heat limit have the uniform large-w asymptotics ES10-ES15.
On the fixed-c integral family, all four first singular corrections are 18, -3/2, -41/4, 11/4; the determinant correction is 9/p and p^3 s4^2=32+176/p+O_c(p^-2).
Every nonzero scalar observation falls into exactly one of four annihilation tiers with powers 0, 2, 3, or 15; both tail first corrections and the two-row observed heat limit are explicit.

The soft eigenvalue and observation hierarchy persist under fixed positive label and receiving metrics, and composition with a fixed invertible conductor has the exact directional error denominator of ES37.
Every hard prime has an integral witness to which the receiver theorems apply.
